newsitem.title: INDIA: India NOCIL Apr-Aug 1996 sales up.
newsitem.headline: India NOCIL Apr-Aug 1996 sales up.

text.p: Sales of National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd (NOCIL) rose to 5.03 billion rupees in the first five months of 1996/97 (April-March) from 4.85 billion in the year-ago period, its chief said on Tuesday.
Exports during the latest period was down at 320 million rupees against 370 million rupees in the same period last year, chairman Arvind Mafatlal told shareholders.
He said profit margins were under pressure due to rising input costs, caused by higher petroleum product prices for naphtha, and lower polymer prices.

The production of ethylene/propylene was higher at 50,924 tonnes during April to August against 48,246 tonnes in the same period a year ago, and rubber chemicals rose to 5,360 tonnes against 5,084 tonnes.
But the output of polymers fell to 26,603 tonnes from 27,070 tonnes, he said.
Mafatlal said the company was seeking foreign partners for financial and technological inputs to implement its 46-billion-rupee expansion programme.
